overview: This file documents the Allied occupation authorities’ late-1947 and early-1948 liberalization and geographic expansion of Japan’s overseas radiotelephone service. It contains U.S. Political Adviser despatches transmitting SCAP directives, duplicate filed copies of SCAPIN 1830 and its rate enclosure, explanatory memoranda for occupation personnel, and SCAPIN 1830/1 extending service to Canada, Cuba, and Mexico and enabling incoming calls to several Japanese cities. Collect calls, transactional and conference calls, permitted currencies, report charges, technical control, accounting procedures, and the precise division of revenue among Japanese and North American carriers are all addressed.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1454 transmitting SCAPIN 1830
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser in Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits the occupation directive revising Japanese overseas radiotelephone service and authorizing service between Japan and Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 1454 forwards SCAPIN 1830 (Dec. 1947), covering new Japan-Hawaii service, rates, and limited transactional calls.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1830 on Japanese overseas radiotelephone service, first copy
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers; R. M. Levy, Adjutant General
subfiles.about: Revises the authorization, operation, charging, accounting, and technical regulation of Japan’s overseas radiotelephone service.
subfiles.summary: SCAPIN 1830 authorizes prepaid Japan-U.S./Hawaii calls, collect calls to the U.S. from January 1948, immediate limited transactional calls, and conference calls, with report-charge and currency accounting rules, retaining military control over operations and equipment.

subfiles.title: Rates and division of revenue for SCAPIN 1830, first copy
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Sets rates, surcharges, report charges, geographic groups, and carrier revenue shares for calls between Japan, the United States, and Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: Rate schedule sets Japan-U.S./Hawaii calls at $12 weekday/$9 Sunday for three minutes, with overtime, conference, and report charges, dividing revenue among Japan's Ministry, AT&T, and (for Hawaii) Mutual Telephone Company by zone.

subfiles.title: General information memorandum concerning SCAPIN 1830, first copy
subfiles.from: M. F. Noyes, Assistant Adjutant General
subfiles.to: All concerned, excluding the Japanese Government
subfiles.about: Explains the policy reasons and practical effects of SCAPIN 1830 for occupation authorities.
subfiles.summary: Memo announces Japan-Hawaii service from December 1947, collect U.S. calls from January 1948, open transactional service, and Sunday rates based on prewar Mutual Telephone tariffs.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1830 on Japanese overseas radiotelephone service, duplicate copy
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers; R. M. Levy, Adjutant General
subfiles.to: Japanese Government, through the Central Liaison Office, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Provides a second filed copy of the directive revising Japanese overseas radiotelephone service.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate SCAPIN 1830 repeats authorizing prepaid Japan-U.S./Hawaii calls, collect and conference calls, and transactional traffic, with accounting and technical rules, this copy preserving the full header and noting transmission via the Central Liaison Office.

subfiles.title: Rates and division of revenue for SCAPIN 1830, duplicate copy
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Provides a second filed copy of the rate and carrier-revenue schedule attached to SCAPIN 1830.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate rate schedule repeats weekday/Sunday/overtime/conference/report charges for Japan-U.S.-Hawaii calls, allocating revenue among the Ministry, AT&T, and Mutual Telephone by zone, and records the Hawaii report charge cut from $1.25 to $0.75 on January 1, 1948.

subfiles.title: General information memorandum concerning SCAPIN 1830, duplicate copy
subfiles.from: M. F. Noyes, Assistant Adjutant General
subfiles.to: All concerned, excluding the Japanese Government
subfiles.about: Provides a second filed copy of the explanatory memorandum accompanying SCAPIN 1830.
subfiles.summary: Memo on SCAPIN 1830 duplicate: Hawaii service opens, with other connections planned, collect calls, transactional traffic, and Mutual Telephone-based Sunday rates; occupation forces must ensure ministry compliance.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 111 transmitting SCAPIN 1830/1
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits the directive extending Japanese radiotelephone service to Canada, Cuba, and Mexico.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 111 forwards SCAPIN 1830/1 (Feb. 1948), extending radiotelephone service to Canada, Cuba, and Mexico with applicable rates and procedures.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1830/1 extending overseas radiotelephone service
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers; R. M. Levy, Adjutant General
subfiles.about: Authorizes outgoing calls to Canada, Cuba, and Mexico and incoming overseas calls to Tokyo and eight additional Japanese cities.
subfiles.summary: SCAPIN 1830/1 authorizes phased prepaid Japan-Canada/Cuba/Mexico calls from February 15, incoming U.S./Hawaii calls to Tokyo from February 10 and other cities by February 20, with AT&T collection and Treasury deposit procedures.

subfiles.title: Revenue schedule for Japan–Canada, Cuba, and Mexico calls
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Specifies weekday and Sunday rates and revenue shares for calls between Japanese zones and Canada, Cuba, and Mexico.
subfiles.summary: Schedule divides Japan into Zone A and B, setting rates and extension-haul deductions for Canada, Cuba, and Mexico calls, sharing revenue between Japan and AT&T, with a shared $0.75 report charge.

subfiles.title: General information memorandum concerning SCAPIN 1830/1
subfiles.from: A. J. Rehe, Assistant Adjutant General
subfiles.to: All concerned, excluding the Japanese Government
subfiles.about: Explains the implementation and routing of expanded incoming radiotelephone service to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Memo summarizes the February timetable for Canada/Cuba/Mexico calls, routing occupation personnel through special booths and others via private phones or Ministry-arranged summons, under continuing technical liaison.

interest: Shows occupation telecommunications reopening from strict control to transactional Japan-Hawaii-U.S. calls, with detailed revenue-sharing tariffs.
